title: Prove sharp global precision for a nested border (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. A synthetic nested triangular border has an exact oracle-precision minimum:

```text
d>=1, P>=1, epsilon=2^(-s), integer s>=1
minimum p = (d+1)P+d, uniquely attained at s=P+1
```

Every exact completed subcall is an involution, stays within 2epsilon of its target and has spectral condition number below four. A chronological prefix still amplifies a permitted inner-call error by epsilon^(-d). Thus completed-subcall accuracy and conditioning alone do not fund recursive precision.

This takes Dillon Amburgey / dillona's PR4623 recursive-precision opening, with its native/compiler/precision lineage credited. Its finite global lemma already requires global bounds. The new template, sharp error formula, minimax proof and checker are the contribution. No predecessor scientific executable or receipt is audited or replayed.

[Proof and package](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/tree/635b2f582549bd511cd8bb9f55e07f6987145643/research/nested-border-precision). [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19372669). Canonical base 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. Only six additive package files change.

## Evidence

- Before: PR4623 leaves a legally flattened recursive caller and its global precision budget open. After: an independently specified fixed two-register word has a sharp all-depth precision law, despite uniformly bounded completed-call condition numbers. This is a contract counterexample, not an assertion that the predecessor's actual caller fails.
- Exact checks pass for 192 matrix fixtures; all 4,400 input/error-sign corner executions on 275 fixtures; 4,055 parameter/precision choices across 30 finite minima; 384 sharp sufficient/one-bit-short families; and thirteen domain or semantic controls. Domains overlap. The universal quantifiers rest on the written proof.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15. Each was timed separately at about 0.12 seconds, below its 120-second timeout. These are timeout observations, not performance comparisons.
- Metadata, committed bytes, source ancestry and executable modes pass at head 635b2f582549bd511cd8bb9f55e07f6987145643. Official export integrity/input coverage and normal/optimized read-only Git-free replays pass. All seven exported files remain hash-identical; two output-location/overwrite controls reject. In-memory syntax and AST checks pass.

From the worktree root, with the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/nested-border-precision/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/nested-border-precision/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/nested-border-precision
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/nested-border-precision --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Substitute another CPython 3.12 path elsewhere. Expected markers are PASS_NESTED_BORDER_PRECISION, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. The direct verifier generates a six-file SHA256 receipt and writes nothing by default.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The minimum fixes one uniform reciprocal-power-of-two parameter, one inner normwise relative-error contract and exact surrounding scale/ADD operations. It optimizes the guarantee against every allowed oracle error; an exact reflection implementation can evade that error. Nonuniform parameters, componentwise accuracy, different algorithms and arbitrary border compilers are outside the minimum.

This is a synthetic real two-register template, not PR4623's literal controller or a source-bound native supplier. Actual native realization, chronological caller integration, a complete target/paid bill, physical scaling/ADD costs, dirty auxiliaries, stock/tape, analytic recovery and all-size multiplication remain unrun. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No new kappa, selected-frontier change, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review or formal proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. No required local check is deferred solely to CI.

## Open next questions

1. Extract one legally flattened approximate controller's chronological scale exponents and actual numerical error contracts, then compare its global precision with the complete paid bill. The source adapter and physical prices remain missing.
2. Prove a concrete componentwise error contract preventing transfer from the enlarged first coordinate into the unscaled second coordinate. The normwise contract alone permits it.

## Related open work

No open PR in the inspected searches studies this exact nested template or computes its precision minimum. Closest open work:

- PR6402 computes ordinary tensor endpoint error for square-zero defects. This uses chronological nesting with a numerical inner call; no tensor-error number is compared or generalized.
- PR6400 concerns exact repair cuts in PR6398's fixed five-call border. This studies a different recursive word and approximate numerical guarantees, with no repair-count comparison.
- PR6468 optimizes scale span and grid transfer for a weighted cyclic recurrence. This fixes a nested word and jointly funds leakage and an inner oracle error; it computes no cyclic balancing optimum.
- PR6602 bounds error from a fixed absolute rounded inverse oracle for arbitrary query algorithms. This uses a relative-error contract inside one specified nested program and computes no inverse-oracle minimax radius.

Live claims, account contributions, reservations, main README and merged/general-form searches were refreshed before committing. The cached helper covered 545 open PRs and 6,571 Discussion records with reported complete pagination; its local scan covered 145 of 8,917 note files. Separate Git searches covered omitted main README text. Cached snapshots, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain limits; searches are not a novelty certificate. 

Completion refresh screened the two other open account contributions created since the CLAIM: PR6602 and PR6603. PR6602 is the distinct oracle model listed above; PR6603 studies seven-source four-root connector incidence. Neither reports a competing value for this nested template. No additional mathematical computation checked those results.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at exact head `635b2f582549bd511cd8bb9f55e07f6987145643` in [run 41628468921](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41628468921): [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41628468921/job/125891695965) and [replay (research/nested-border-precision)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41628468921/job/125893809388). The completed checks were read once with `gh pr checks 6604 --repo CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds`; separate run metadata confirms completed success and the matching head.

Both registered normal/optimized commands and the local scientific, committed-source and portable-export checks passed. Hosted replay certifies execution of the declared finite checks and source validation. Independent human and formal proof-kernel acceptance of the universal written proof remain unclaimed. No CI failure or deferred required local check remains.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Six additive files in one opt-in package.

**Blast Radius:** isolated. Shared code, frozen predecessors, upstream and selected-frontier files are unchanged.
